CompoNet grows without limit, can choose among old policies state by state, and has standard-benchmark numbers. It is the continual-RL baseline reviewers will expect next to PNN for any chain claim.

defensible_claims: The construction itself. Four targeted searches (isolation, null space, readout, robotics) found no method that adds per-skill residual adapters to a frozen deep policy and projects their post-nonlinearity writes onto the joint null space of all earlier linear action heads. Under this construction, every earlier skill's action mean is unchanged at every state, including states first reached in closed loop after the change (measured maximum deviation about 1e-6). It needs no stored data, works with any optimiser, and uses one fixed-width vector that all heads read. Present it as making Peng & Risteski's linear-case rule exact for deep nonlinear policies through growth, not as a new principle.

The Pick->Stack result (ManiSkill3 PickCube->StackCube, PPO, sparse reward, 3 seeds, 90% criterion). Pick stays at the expert's 0.992-0.996. Stack reaches 90% in 1.13M steps with an adapter of about 142k parameters (about +100% of the 142.6k-parameter trunk), in 1.30M with about 36k (+25%), and in 1.77M with about 9k (+6%). For comparison: full fine-tuning takes 1.50M and Pick drops to 0.82-0.86; closed-loop KL distillation takes 2.76M with Pick at 0.99; head-only takes 3.1M. At equal added parameters it beats FT-N (fine-tune a copy, also exact, 1.50M) on this pair.

The closed-loop finding on this pair: first-order protection of the shared weights does not translate into retention. Projecting both the gradient and the Adam step with a Kronecker block cut drift on stored states from 10 to 3.8, yet Pick success stayed at 0.80. Every failure happens after the grasp, and after the grasp the student's error on its own states is 2.2x its error on the teacher's states. Drift on stored states is therefore not a proxy for retention. Add the GPM claim only after the gradient-projected gpm095g run and the FN-PPO arms finish.

Data-free versus data-based retention. Unlike KL/BC distillation and replay (Wolczyk et al., ICML 2024; ACCRUE, arXiv 2610.18596; both searcher-confirmed, not independently verified), the guarantee does not depend on which states were stored or rolled out. This matters because forgetting concentrates in states the old skill reaches only after the change.

The exactness conditions hold in this code base. Each head is a linear readout of the stream with nothing after the writes, and wrwl/ppo.py has no running observation normaliser. Each skill's critic is a separate network (the official ManiSkill Agent layout) that never reads the stream, so 8 protected rows per 8-D action skill are the whole capacity cost.

Conditional, after the chain runs: suppose later skills reach 90% faster by reading earlier adapters' writes than side-tuning does (side-tuning has no reuse), and match PNN or concatenation with fewer parameters at fixed width. Then 'a write-protected fixed-width skill stream gives forward transfer without growth' becomes the main defensible claim.
claims_to_avoid: 'First method that adds skills without forgetting' or 'first exact retention in closed loop'. Progressive Nets (and the CoRL 2017 robot version), Side-Tuning, Ternary Feature Masks and CompoNet (all verified) already keep old tasks exactly at every state with no data, by freezing or isolation. So do PackNet and TAIL (both searcher-confirmed).

That the null-space principle is new or discovered here. Verified prior work: Peng & Risteski 2022 (exact null space of all earlier heads in a shared fixed-width vector, with random seeding of new directions) and Anthes et al. 2024 (readout range vs null space). Searcher-confirmed: Shan, Li & Sompolinsky (PNAS 2026), output-null activity in motor cortex (Kaufman et al. 2014), and task-priority null-space control (Siciliano & Slotine 1991). Say 'output-side' only together with 'exact for deep nonlinear policies'.

That the projection is what keeps old skills, or what enables reuse. Freezing plus linear per-skill heads keeps old skills. Prefix-sum (head j reads h0+g1+...+gj) and concatenation keep old skills bitwise exact and reuse earlier adapters without any projection.

'Parameter-efficient'. At +6-100% of the trunk per skill (9k-142k parameters), NSA is heavy next to per-task LoRA (about 1-2% in TAIL, searcher-confirmed). Only claim parameter-matched comparisons, and report absolute counts.

'Faster than fine-tuning' or 'scales to many skills' in general. So far there is one pair, 3 seeds, and k=2. A width-256 stream caps at about 31 skills with 8-D actions, and confining learning to a shrinking subspace may hurt new skills (anterograde interference, Shan et al., searcher-confirmed).

That starting the adapter random rather than zero is a finding. DPGrad already seeds new directions randomly, and PNN's CoRL 2017 initialisation (copied old head, zero weights on new features, random new module) is the same idea. Also, only an all-zero adapter stays dead. With a zero last layer, the copied head picks up null-space weights from the trunk's own activity after one update, and the adapter then gets gradient. That is an inference from the gradient algebra; check it with one run before stating anything.

'Approximate or first-order protection fails in closed loop' as a general law. It has been shown on one pair. The Adam confound that SGP reported is already handled (--protect_grad), but the gradient-projected GPM (gpm095g) and FN-PPO arms must finish. 'Isolation beats regularisation' is also already known in continual RL (Continual World results as tabulated by CSP and CompoNet). State it as a measured closed-loop finding on manipulation pairs.

That FN-PPO is a new algorithm. Projecting updates away from the old skill's output-gradient subspace, estimated on old-task states and re-estimated during training with Adam re-projected, is Anthes et al.'s deep variant (verified) and belongs to the OGD/GPM/SGP family. Present it as the parameter-free baseline with closed-loop anchors.

That it applies to VLAs, diffusion or flow action heads, or any shared nonlinear consumer. Exactness needs every protected readout to be linear in the stream, with no LayerNorm or nonlinearity after the writes, and any shared observation or feature normaliser frozen per skill.

The name 'NSA', or an undefined 'null space'. NSA collides with Native Sparse Attention (ACL 2025) and is close to NuSA-CL (ICLR 2026, weight-space 'null space adaptation'). RSS readers also hear 'null space' as task-priority control. Rename it (e.g. 'output-null skill adapters' or 'write-protected skill stream') and define the term in the paper.

required_baselines.name: Prefix-sum adapters with no projection (residual form of Progressive Prompts / PNN)
required_baselines.why: The decisive ablation. With known skill IDs and linear heads, letting head j read its own prefix h0+g1+...+gj keeps old skills bitwise exact, reuses every earlier adapter and spends no dimensions. It isolates what the projection itself buys. If it ties NSA, drop the projection from the headline. (Progressive Prompts, ICLR 2023, searcher-confirmed.)
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: In wrwl/nsa.py, add a switch that sets the `null` buffer to the identity and zero-initialises the adapter's last Linear, so the copied head still starts as the old policy. Evaluate skill j through feat.level(j) instead of the last level; scripts/nsa_eval.py's own(level) already does this. Run widths 16/64/256 on Pick->StackCubeNarrow with the nsa256 recipe from scripts/run_protect.sh (gripper floor 1.0, 1024 envs, sparse reward, stop after 3 evals >= 0.9), with at least 3 seeds. Also add a chain64-noproj arm to scripts/run_chain.sh. The chain64p start (Pick's head reading Stack's adapter) cannot be exact without the projection; record that as NSA's one structural edge over this baseline.

required_baselines.name: Side-tuning: a private adapter feeding only the new head
required_baselines.why: Verified prior work. For one new skill, NSA is side-tuning. In a chain, side-tuning has no reuse of earlier adapters, so chain-vs-side-tuning measures forward transfer through the stream.
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: Head k reads h0 + g_k(x, h2), with g_k's last layer zero-initialised and no projection; earlier heads read their own private sums. Use the same widths and seeds. In scripts/run_chain.sh, run it next to chain64, chain64p and the existing place_nsa64 arm (one level straight from Pick).

required_baselines.name: Concatenation (PNN-lite) and a parameter-matched Progressive Net column
required_baselines.why: NSA equals concatenation [h0; g1; ...; gk] with tied head weights, so concatenation bounds NSA's expressivity from above. PNN, including the CoRL 2017 robot version with the same head-copy start, is the canonical freeze-and-add method with chained reuse, and reviewers will ask for it by name.
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: (a) Concatenation: a trunk module that returns torch.cat([h0, g1, ..., gk]). The new head is Linear(256+sum(w), 8), initialised to [W_copy, 0, ..., 0]; adapters start random, and old heads read only their own blocks. (b) PNN: for each skill, a narrow 3-layer tanh column with lateral Linear maps from the frozen trunk's layers and from earlier columns. The head reads [h0; column_k], with the old head's weights copied and zeros on the new column (the CoRL 2017 initialisation). Pick column widths so the column plus its laterals matches the 9k/36k/142k parameters of NSA widths 16/64/256, and report the counts.

required_baselines.name: CompoNet (Malagon et al., ICML 2024)
required_baselines.why: A verified continual-RL isolation method with exact retention and policy reuse through action outputs. Public code; it is the continual-RL comparison reviewers will expect for chains.
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: Port the module from github.com/mikelma/componet into actor_mean. Each skill's module runs output and input attention over the frozen earlier skills' mean actions (the Pick expert, then Stack's head) on the 42-d state, plus its internal MLP residual. Train it with wrwl/ppo.py's PPO on the same recipe (CompoNet itself used PPO on ALE). Report its parameters per skill, about one trunk.

required_baselines.name: FT-N (fine-tune a copy) and full fine-tuning
required_baselines.why: FT-N is the simplest exact baseline: keep the old network and fine-tune a copy, adding one network per skill. It is the fair parameter-matched comparison for NSA width 256. Full FT is the forgetting reference. Both appear in CompoNet's tables.
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: Already run: the monitor arm of scripts/run_protect.sh (1.50M steps; Pick drops to 0.82-0.86 when read through the shared layers). FT-N is the same run with Pick kept as its own network: retention is exact and each skill adds one actor (about 145k parameters). For chains, use the ftchain arm of scripts/run_chain.sh and report it both ways.

required_baselines.name: Per-skill LoRA on the trunk (TAIL; PPO LoRA policy library)
required_baselines.why: The standard parameter-efficient isolation baseline in robot learning: TAIL (ICLR 2024) and a LoRA policy library trained with PPO on Meta-World (arXiv 2606.25700, unreviewed); both searcher-confirmed, not independently verified. Swapping adapters gives exact retention at about 1-2% of parameters, so this tests whether NSA's +6-100% is needed.
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: Wrap the three trunk Linear layers with rank-r LoRA (B zero, A random) and copy the old head for the new skill. Run the old skill with its LoRA switched off, which is exact. Each unit of rank costs 1,322 parameters, so ranks 1/4/16/27 give about 1%/4%/15%/25% of the trunk. In chains, initialise skill k's LoRA from skill k-1's (as TAIL does) and also from scratch.

required_baselines.name: PackNet (fixed-capacity exact isolation)
required_baselines.why: The fixed-capacity competitor to NSA's fixed-width claim: exact, data-free retention inside a network that does not grow. It tops CSP's CW10 table and is a standard LIBERO lifelong-learning baseline (searcher-confirmed).
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: Prune the Pick trunk to its top 50% or 25% of weights by magnitude, then re-tune Pick briefly with PPO on PickCube with the pruned weights held at zero. Train Stack only on the freed weights, using element-wise gradient masks (generalise the row masks behind --train_units), and evaluate Pick under its own mask. The existing 20%-random-units arm (1.75M steps, Pick 0.96-0.98) is the non-exact variant.

required_baselines.name: KL/BC distillation to the old policy (Wolczyk et al., ICML 2024)
required_baselines.why: The strongest data-based retention baseline for RL fine-tuning (searcher-confirmed). NSA's selling point is exactness without stored or rolled-out states, at a better speed.
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: Already run: distill1d in scripts/run_protect.sh (closed-loop states, coefficient 1: 2.76M steps, Pick 0.99). Add the stored-state arms distill01 and distill1, and klcl1/klcl3, each with at least 3 seeds, to show the whole speed-retention frontier rather than one coefficient.

required_baselines.name: FN-PPO and first-order projections (no added parameters)
required_baselines.why: The parameter-free comparison the user chose. Closest precedents: Anthes et al.'s deep functional null space (verified), Duncker et al.'s two-sided projection, and GPM/SGP (SGP also found that under PPO the projection must be applied after Adam). It shows what exactness by growth buys over approximate protection anchored on states.
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: Use the run_protect.sh arms fncl, fnbank and fncl_w5 (PROT_DIR=runs/protect_3m, 3M steps, a checkpoint at every eval), plus block09g and gpm095g with both gradient and step projected. Report t90, the retention curve from old_eval.csv, and the pre- vs post-grasp error ratio from scripts/forgetting_closedloop.py.

required_baselines.name: Head-only on the frozen stream
required_baselines.why: The lower bound that shows what new capacity buys (3.1M steps). In chains, head-only learning on the accumulated stream measures the library effect.
required_baselines.how_to_run_here: --freeze_trunk --init_ckpt=PICK, already run. For chains, add a small flag to wrwl/ppo.py that trains only a new head (with its own log-std) on the last level's stream of an --nsa_base checkpoint.

experiments_that_would_make_it_novel: Projection ablation with a pre-registered rule; run it first, before writing the abstract. Compare NSA, prefix-sum (no projection), concatenation and side-tuning at adapter widths 16/64/256, on Pick->Stack and on Pick->Stack->Place, with 5 seeds. Measure t90 at the 90% criterion, with an eval every 102,400 steps. Rule: if prefix-sum or concatenation is within one eval interval of NSA's median t90 in both settings, treat the projection as an implementation detail and pitch the paper as a fixed-width progressive network. If NSA is clearly faster, test the 'protected scaffold' explanation: the projection keeps the directions the copied head reads intact while the adapter learns. To test it, log the new head's grasp-phase action drift over the first 0.3M steps in each arm.

A 4-5-skill chain in Pick's observation layout: Pick -> Stack -> Place, plus two more skills (e.g. PushRetreat or PushCubeDir directions mapped into the layout, or place-and-release variants). Report four things for each skill. (1) t90. (2) Exact retention of every earlier skill through the last level (maximum action deviation from scripts/nsa_eval.py). (3) Forward transfer: t90 when the new head reads all earlier adapters, versus one level straight from Pick (the chain64p vs place_nsa64 design, repeated for every skill). (4) Added parameters. Compare against side-tuning, prefix-sum, concatenation, PNN, CompoNet, per-skill LoRA, PackNet, FT-N and FT. The result that would carry the paper: positive transfer that side-tuning lacks, at fewer parameters than PNN.

Capacity curve. Run a long, cheap chain of 10-30 skills (e.g. PushCubeDir at different angles, or PickCube with different goal regions) and plot three things: t90 against k as the free width 256-8k shrinks; the effective rank each adapter actually writes; and the k at which NSA falls behind concatenation, which has no capacity budget. This answers 'what happens at skill 30?' and tests, in RL, the anterograde-interference warning of Shan, Li & Sompolinsky (PNAS 2026, searcher-confirmed).

Library effect. After each of k skills, learn a held-out skill head-only on the accumulated stream and plot its t90 against k. If head-only learning on the stream approaches adapter speed as k grows, the fixed-width shared stream has a concrete payoff; concatenation can match it only with a growing head input.

Order and source robustness. Run reversed pairs (a Stack or Place expert gaining Pick) and 3 independently trained source experts, as the earlier plan review required. This shows the speed-up is not specific to pairs where the new skill is the old skill plus a release.

a2r Isaac Lab pair: insert_key insert -> insert+turn, run from our own runtime copy (Piper X, point clouds, PPO, deterministic evals of 1024-2048 episodes, 3-seed paired confidence intervals as in a2r E-13). Put the stream at the last hidden layer before a linear action-mean head. Check that no LayerNorm or nonlinearity follows the writes and that any observation normaliser is frozen per skill. Compare with full FT, FT-N, closed-loop KL distillation, FN-PPO, and an ACCRUE-style arm with a residual actor plus distillation (ACCRUE, arXiv 2610.18596, searcher-confirmed). RSS reviewers will weigh this experiment most.

A consumer that needs one vector. Give every skill a linear termination (or success) head whose rows join the protected set. Then run Pick -> Stack -> Place as one long-horizon task, switching heads on termination, from a single forward pass. Show that every action head and termination signal stays exact as skills are added. Without such a consumer the shared vector is an implementation detail; with it, it is a feature.

Closed-loop forgetting analysis as the motivating figure, not the headline, on both pairs. For FN-PPO, for block and GPM projection with both gradient and step projected, and for KL distillation, plot Pick retention against drift on stored states. Also plot the ratio of the student's error on its own states to its error on the teacher's states, before versus after the grasp (scripts/forgetting_closedloop.py).
synthesis.framing: Pitch a robotics problem and a training recipe, not a new null-space method, and drop the name NSA. A possible title: 'Skills that stay put: adding RL skills to one robot policy with exact, data-free retention'. The problem: a deployed policy must gain skills (pick, then stack, then place, then insert-and-turn) without changing what it already does at any state it can reach after the change. The preliminary closed-loop analysis shows why protecting stored states cannot promise this. Projecting both gradient and step cut stored-state drift from 10 to 3.8, yet Pick success stayed at 0.80. Every failure came after the grasp, and the student's errors on its own states were 2.2x those on the teacher's. The method: freeze the trunk and heads, give each new skill a small adapter that writes into one fixed-width stream only where no earlier head reads, and start the new head as a copy of the closest skill. Say openly that this is the growth-based escape from Peng & Risteski's impossibility result for fixed-capacity learners, and a fixed-width cousin of progressive nets and side-tuning. For RSS readers, describe it as task-priority null-space control (Siciliano & Slotine 1991) moved from joint space into feature space, with old skills at strict priority. Preliminary results: Pick stays at the expert's 0.99 while Stack learns faster than full fine-tuning, FT-N and closed-loop KL distillation, with FN-PPO as the parameter-free comparison. Stage-2 hypotheses, pre-registered at the 90% criterion: (H1) write protection, not just freezing plus extra capacity, speeds learning, tested against prefix-sum, concatenation and side-tuning at matched width; (H2) in 4-5-skill chains, later skills learn faster by reading earlier adapters at fixed width, tested against PNN, CompoNet, per-skill LoRA and PackNet; (H3) the recipe carries over to a2r's Isaac Lab insertion pair. The neuroscience link is real but belongs in one sentence of motivation, not as evidence. Motor cortex keeps preparatory activity in 'output-null' dimensions that its downstream readout cannot see (Kaufman et al., Nat. Neurosci. 2014). After monkeys learned a new BCI decoder, the trace of that learning sat mainly in the familiar decoder's output-null dimensions while the old behaviour stayed proficient (Losey et al., Curr. Biol. 2024). Both are searcher-confirmed, not independently verified. Finally, pre-empt the counter-narrative that large pretrained VLAs forget little under LoRA RL (Hu et al., RLC 2026, searcher-confirmed). Scope the claim to small RL-trained policies, where that same study and your own full-FT run show large forgetting, and argue that exactness matters for long skill chains and for certifying deployed behaviour.
